title: Introduce init-throttle-curves and values translation layer for safe upgrades
author: Priya Rao
description:
Background: private installer customers run tenant-heavy init workflows during installs and upgrades. We observed that a flat concurrency cap or simple backoff causes noisy resource spikes and long tail completion times for large clusters. This PR introduces a lightweight, declarative init-throttle-curves concept (time-series shaped concurrency targets) and a values translation layer to map older values schemas to the new shape during upgrades so existing installs can opt into the new behavior without manual edits.

What I changed: added a new values schema (charts/private/values.schema.json) and server-side translator job that runs as part of the upgrade path to convert legacy init concurrency and rate settings into a throttle curve. Implemented template helpers to render the curve into init-job annotations and sidecar indexers; extended helm templates to support curve-driven pacing, jitter, and tenant priorities. Also added a Terraform module mapping so operator IaC can pass either legacy or curve values. Updated docs and the upgrade guide with examples and recommended safe defaults.

Design highlights: the throttle curve is an ordered list of {duration, concurrency} points expressed in values.yaml. The template produces a small sidecar config consumed by the init worker which enforces soft concurrency targets and exponential smoothing for transient bursts. The translation layer handles three legacy shapes (static-concurrency, percent-of-nodes, burst-window) and emits a conservative curve by default. No breaking API: old values continue to work, new values are additive.

Compatibility/migration: a pre-upgrade check is added that scans values and, if legacy keys are present, creates a Kubernetes Job (installer-values-translate) that writes the derived values into a namespaced configmap and annotates the Helm release with migration metadata. This gives operators a chance to review generated curves before commit. For fully-automated upgrades operators can enable auto-apply in the installer profile.

Testing and validation: local k3s integration runs with 50 simulated tenants, unit helm template tests for three value shapes, and an e2e smoke scenario on a small GCP cluster. Metrics and tracing hooks were exercised to verify the smoothing behavior reduces peak pod churn in synthetic workloads.

Checklist: 
- [x] values.schema.json with validation
- [x] template helpers and annotated init job templates
- [x] translation Job and configmap flow for upgrades
- [x] Terraform mapping updates and example profile
- [x] docs (docs/private/upgrade-init-throttle.md) and examples
- [x] helm unit tests and CI pipeline integration

Why this change: improves cluster stability during installs/upgrades for tenants-heavy clusters and provides a safe upgrade path so operators can adopt gradual rollout of the feature with visibility and rollback guardrails.

Notes: kept the translation deterministic (no external network calls) and idempotent. Default curve for new installs is conservative (ramp to 25% concurrency over 10 minutes then plateau) to avoid surprise resource spikes.

release_notes:
- Add init-throttle-curves (ramp-shaped concurrency profiles) for installer init jobs
- Provide values translation Job to convert legacy concurrency settings to curves during upgrade
- Terraform module mapping added for backward compatibility
- Default behavior is conservative to avoid resource spikes
